title: Finding black neighborhoods, road trips and $500 in Shreveport
summary: Where they stayed on the road, mostly overnight gigs, and Abbe Goldberg booking $500 dates in Shreveport after When I Meet My Girl.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Do you have problems checking in the hotels or, you know?

Well, we did, now how we did, whenever we had to live in, you know, in places, we knew how to find the black part of town. And, well, this is what we looked for anyway, because we wanted to have fun. So we would always look for the black part of town, go check in, and then find where we were going to play. But most of our things was overnight. You didn't do a lot of... No, no. No, no. Now, you know, the early 50s was when I did a lot of, you know, we would go. Like we stayed in Nashville. We stayed in Washington, D.C. We stayed in Baltimore, Maryland. You know, and played out of that town. Made all the towns within about two, three hundred mile radius. But other than that, you know, like we play Shreveport. I leave here in the morning. We play Shreveport a night. And sometimes we would play two nights. Now Mr. Abbe Goldberg used to book us in Shreveport, and we played at the Cross Lake Country Club, and we played probably at Downtown Hotel. And you know how much money I was getting there? Which year is it? This is 1958, 59.
I got $500, that was a big, oh that was big time.

Yeah, seven people, seven people, and transportation. And that was big money, $500, because I have no shell booking agency that booked me in Shreveport. See that was off when I meet my girl, and it was $500. Whole pile of money.
And you had to give a percentage to your agent? Oh yeah.
Yeah. Well they had already had it because they got deposit money. See they got deposit.
And whatever was left over the deposit.
So, but you know, even at that, making, you know, well a dollar was 100% better than what it is now. It was always a pretty fair living.
